cases.basis: No TCL page found that maps Q6C to C6K: the Gulf support page exists for 98C6K, and tcl.com/gulf has no 98Q6C page (404). Independent spec databases and a reviewer list Q6C as an alias of C6K, with the same hardware: 98in, 512 zones, HVA, 144Hz game mode, Onkyo 2.1 with subwoofer, 2025. TCL's own UK Q6C launch gives a zone ladder (180/242/312/420/512 for 55-98in) that matches C6K. Not high confidence because the main source is a spec database and there is no TCL cross-reference. The Noon/Jarir 120Hz-vs-144Hz labels are different ways of describing one panel (100/120Hz native, 144Hz game mode), not different hardware.

cases.basis: The two codes come from different Hisense generations and market lines. Hisense Spain's own page gives 55E7S PRO as a 2026 European model (E7 PRO series, MT9618, BT 5.4, EAN 6942351432779). Hisense's year letters are N=2024 and Q=2025. On that reading, Q72Q is a 2025 Middle-East Q7-family variant, sold at Carrefour KSA as 65Q72Q. Hisense ME lists the 2026 Q7 line separately as 'Q7S' and the 2025 one as 'Q7Q'. I found no manufacturer or distributor source that names 55Q72Q as an alias of 55E7S PRO. Not high confidence because I found no official Hisense spec sheet for 55Q72Q itself, and the year comes from the naming convention. eXtra's 55Q7EQ is another code I could not find anywhere else, so it adds no evidence.

cases.basis: I found 85Q6EQ nowhere except the eXtra claim: not on any Hisense site, distributor page, or second merchant. 85Q6Q is a real 2025 Hisense 85in QLED 60Hz model, listed by Hisense South Africa and by GCC retailers. Hisense ME lists a Q6 line with an 85in size but gives no suffix variants. I found nothing showing that an 'E' before the year letter marks an export or regional version of the same set, or that 85Q6EQ is a typo. eXtra also shows a matching unexplained '55Q7EQ' code, which suggests an eXtra-specific code, but that proves neither SAME nor DIFFERENT.
